evals.name: empty-args-routes-to-deepening
evals.expected_output: Empty args route to the deepening lens (not a missing-action error). Reads the nearest project glossary (if any) and relevant architecture decision records, walks the codebase via the Explore subagent, applies the deletion test, and writes BOTH the HTML report and the machine-readable candidate artifact before asking which candidate to explore.
expectations: Routes empty `$ARGUMENTS` to the `deepening` action — does NOT error on a missing/unknown action
Reads the nearest project glossary (if the project maintains one) and any relevant architecture decision records before exploring
Uses the Agent tool with subagent_type=Explore (or an equivalent read-only exploration subagent) to walk the codebase rather than reading inline
Applies the deletion test to anything suspected shallow (concentrates vs moves complexity)

Writes the durable machine-readable candidate artifact (default `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/deepening-candidates-<timestamp>.md`, or the consuming project's work-artifact location, with the path announced) alongside the HTML report
Does NOT propose interfaces in Phase 2; ends by asking which candidate to explore

evals.name: shallow-cluster-classified-strong
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — focus on the order intake path: OrderHandler calls OrderValidator calls OrderRepo, and each is a one-method wrapper that forwards its argument and returns the next call's result. Validation and pricing logic actually live spread across the three.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the OrderHandler->OrderValidator->OrderRepo chain as shallow (interface nearly as complex as implementation). Deletion test returns 'concentrates'. Recommendation badge Strong, dependency category in-process or local-substitutable with the testing strategy tied to it. Candidate written to the candidate artifact with status proposed.
expectations: Identifies the wrapper chain as shallow — interface nearly as complex as the implementation
Deletion-test verdict is 'concentrates complexity' (earning-its-keep / candidate signal), not 'just moves it'
Assigns the recommendation badge Strong for an unambiguous shallow pass-through cluster
Assigns a dependency category (in-process or local-substitutable) and ties the testing strategy to that category per dependencies.md
Uses ONLY deepening vocabulary (module, interface, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) — never component, service, or boundary
Records the candidate in the candidate artifact with status: proposed and a one-sentence problem + one-sentence deepening

evals.name: deep-module-not-over-flagged
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — review the pricing engine: a single Price(order) entry point backed by ~600 lines of rules, tax tables, and rounding policy, with a focused test suite that drives it only through Price(order). An architecture decision record already records keeping the rules in-process.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT propose deepening an already-deep module (small interface, large well-tested implementation). Deletion test shows complexity would only move, not concentrate. If surfaced at all, badge is Speculative with explicit rationale; respects the existing decision record rather than re-litigating it.
expectations: Does NOT recommend deepening a module that is already deep (small interface hiding large, tested behavior)
Deletion-test verdict is 'would just move complexity' — correctly NOT a candidate
If surfaced at all, badge is Speculative with explicit rationale — never Strong
Respects the existing architecture decision record (keep rules in-process); only revisits it if friction is real enough, and marks the conflict clearly if so
Does not invent shallowness where the interface-to-implementation ratio is already favorable

evals.name: design-it-twice-branch-on-selected-candidate
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — I've picked the order intake candidate from the report. Before we lock a shape, show me a few radically different interface designs and tell me which one you'd pick.
evals.expected_output: Enters the Design-It-Twice exploration mode: frames the problem space (constraints, dependency categories, an illustrative sketch labeled not-a-proposal) and shows it to the user first, fans out 3-4 parallel subagents each under a deliberately orthogonal design constraint, presents the five-part designs sequentially, compares on interface depth/leverage, locality of change, and seam placement, and closes with an opinionated recommendation (hybrid allowed).
expectations: Frames the problem space FIRST — constraints any new interface must satisfy, dependency categories, and a small illustrative sketch explicitly labeled as not a proposal — and shows it to the user before any design is produced

Fans out 3-4 subagents in parallel, each under a deliberately orthogonal design constraint (minimal interface, maximum flexibility, optimize the common caller, ports and adapters only when cross-seam dependencies warrant)

Briefs each subagent with the concrete technical context (file paths, coupling details, dependency category, what sits behind the seam) and requires the five-part structured result (interface incl. invariants/error modes; usage example; what the implementation hides; dependency strategy; trade-offs)
Presents the designs sequentially, then compares on exactly three axes: interface depth/leverage, locality of change, and seam placement
Closes with an opinionated recommendation — possibly a hybrid — a strong read, not a menu of equally weighted options

evals.name: resolved-vocabulary-routes-to-owner
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — while grilling the selected candidate we resolved a new project term, Fulfillment Window. /planning:domain-modeling is available in this session. Preserve the term and continue.
evals.expected_output: Invokes /planning:domain-modeling for active glossary maintenance, then resumes the architecture interview. Architecture does not duplicate the glossary contract or discover bounded contexts; when that skill is unavailable it preserves only the consumer-owned fallback.
expectations: Invokes /planning:domain-modeling because the skill is available in the current session
Does not reimplement a glossary filename, location, or entry contract in architecture
Does not perform bounded-context discovery as part of preserving the term
Continues the selected-candidate interview after the glossary update
